title: All Values of an Expression With Any Brackets

concept.title: Choose the operator that is applied last
body: Without brackets, `2*3-4*5` is read with the usual priorities, but here you may **put brackets anywhere** and every different bracketing can give a different value. Think about the **last** operator that is applied. If it is the operator number `k`, then the numbers on its left form one expression and the numbers on its right form another expression, and each of them can again be bracketed in any way.

This is **divide and conquer** by the split point: for every operator, combine every value of the left part with every value of the right part. A set removes equal values, because different bracketings often meet the same result. The number of bracketings of 8 numbers is 429 (a Catalan number), small enough for the plain recursion.

statement: An expression has numbers separated by the operators `+`, `-` and `*`, with no spaces. You may put brackets anywhere, in any way, so that the order of the operations changes. Print all different values that the expression can get, in increasing order, one per line.
inputFormat: The only line has the expression.
outputFormat: The different values in increasing order, one per line.
constraints: The expression has 1 to 8 numbers, each between 0 and 99 (without leading zeros).
All values fit in a 64-bit integer.

examples.note: The five bracketings give 10, -14, -10, -10 and -34, so the different values are -34, -14, -10 and 10.

hints: Pick the last operator to apply: the numbers to its left and right form two smaller expressions.
For every pair (value of the left part, value of the right part) apply the operator.
Keep the values in a set, because different bracketings can give the same value.

explanation: For every choice of the last operator, all values of the left part are combined with all values of the right part. The base case is a single number. A set keeps each value once, and the values are printed in increasing order.
solution.complexity: Time proportional to the Catalan number of the operators (429 for seven operators), space O(that).
